scope_findings.claim: Dr. Rositsa Cholakova undertakes international mobility from Bulgaria (Plovdiv) to Hungary (Budapest, ELTE) for an MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship, satisfying the international mobility and researcher excellence criteria that are the defining scope criteria of the instrument.
The application is submitted jointly by the researcher (Dr. Rositsa Cholakova) and a beneficiary (ELTE) in the academic sector.

The European Fellowship takes place at ELTE, Budapest, Hungary — an EU Member State — satisfying the requirement that EF fellowships must take place in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.
The fellowship duration is confirmed at 24 months, within the 12–24 month range required for European Postdoctoral Fellowships.

A Career Development Plan is prepared jointly by supervisor (Dr. András Jung) and fellow (Dr. Rositsa Cholakova), submitted as a project deliverable at the start of the action (by months 2–3), then reviewed and updated at M12 and M24.

Training integrates digital and AI skills including the responsible use of generative AI in environmental modelling and scientific coding, addressing the MSCA-PF mandatory requirement for key transferable skills including digital ones.

Training integrates knowledge valorisation and innovation/entrepreneurship — specifically translating the uncertainty-aware crop-water decision-support demonstrator toward user uptake — addressing the MSCA-PF requirement for fostering a culture of knowledge valorisation and innovation.

Training integrates research integrity and open-science ethics: FAIR data management, open research software, and reproducible validation; preparing the fellow for increased research collaboration and information-sharing via digital technologies including open access.

A two-way transfer of knowledge is structured: the fellow brings plant-physiology and non-destructive stress-phenotyping expertise into the host's geoinformatics group; the host provides remote-sensing, hyperspectral and multisensor-fusion competences in return, evidenced by at least two methods seminars delivered at the host.

The project develops an uncertainty-aware multi-sensor diagnostic and irrigation decision support framework for tomato crops (Route B: homogeneous patch proxy), fusing Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, PlanetScope high-resolution imagery, ERA5 meteorological reanalysis and field sensor data via probabilistic machine learning to estimate root-zone soil moisture and crop water status.
